title: A mod-p unit Kurihara witness at every good prime p >= 5
statement: For every prime p >= 5 of good reduction for E, including the supersingular primes and 19, 59 and 487, M_infinity(delta) = 0. Hence some squarefree Kato conductor n, which may depend on p, gives a mod-p unit Kurihara witness: delta_n is nonzero mod p. The bad primes 2243, 4547 and 5843 and the primes p <= 3 are not covered.

imports: Castella-Liu-Wan, "Kato's main conjecture for nonordinary modular forms", author-hosted revision dated 2026-09-21 (https://web.math.ucsb.edu/~castella/CLW2.pdf, sha256 0686fa414b242e8e3b1cccd3fe906c8eefcfdb7b568563daa3089701d036fb98), Theorem A, with Lemma 2.10, Remark 2.20 and section 5.6 ((5.18), (5.21)-(5.22)) for the character and the integral normalization: (ram) holds via l = 2243 (v_2243(Delta) = 1, split multiplicative I_1); k = 2 < p; p-regular since a_p = 0 at supersingular p >= 5. The arXiv v1 (2608.29470v1) required squarefree N; the revision does not. At k = 2 the proved component omega^(k/2) = omega is the cyclotomic one for T_pE (Remark 2.20).

Castella-Sano, arXiv:2601.14504v1: Theorem A and Corollary A (with the CLW input at the nonordinary primes) and Theorem B (the ordinary primes); the determinant equivalence of Proposition 2.2.3, with the S-imprimitive Euler factors retained
the retained seed inputs: residual surjectivity at every odd p and p-adic surjectivity at p >= 5 (A.3); the Manin constant divides 2^9 (A.4); Tam = 16 (A.1)
normalization: Kurihara numbers delta_n in Z/I_n as in Castella-Sano section 1.1 (and Kim sections 1.2.2 and 1.4): n runs over squarefree products of primes l not dividing N with l = 1 mod p and a_l = l + 1 mod p (so a_l = 2 mod p); I_n is the sum of the ideals I_l = (l - 1, a_l - l - 1)Z_p; the modular symbols are normalized by the positive Neron period Omega^+_E, the integral over E(R) of omega_E (2*omega_1 for this curve), and weighted by discrete logarithms; M(n) is the p-adic order of delta_n in Z/I_n, M_r = min{M(n) : nu(n) = r}, and M_infinity(delta) is the limit of M_r over r of the parity of the root number. Changing primitive roots multiplies delta_n by a p-unit. These auxiliary primes are not the G2 auxiliaries of B.16.

The Euler factors at 2243 and 5843 are nonunits at these primes (2242 = 2*19*59, 5844 = 12*487); both formulations retain these factors and neither cancels them, so they create no extra exception. The supersingular primes come from the CLW revision, because the supersingular case of Theorem B requires squarefree N.

No rank-zero step of CLW section 5.6 ((5.19), (5.20), (5.23), (5.24)) is used, and no historical E11 or 288 scalar is identified with delta_n: no normalization comparison has been done.

title: The minimal unit-witness length equals the Selmer dimension
statement: For every good prime p >= 5 put r_p := min{nu(n) : delta_n is nonzero mod p}, the minimal length of a mod-p unit Kurihara witness (finite by B.20). Then r_p = dim_{F_p} Sel_p(E/Q); r_p is even and >= 2; and r_p = 2 if and only if Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity] = 0. The equivalence also excludes a hypothetical divisible part: no finiteness of Sha is assumed.

title: The character-depth criterion (strict depth below four)
statement: Let p >= 5 be a good prime, let K/Q be a real cyclic extension of degree p whose actual conductor m is prime to pN (m may be composite), and let chi be a faithful character of Gal(K/Q). If v_{zeta_p - 1}(chi(theta_K^MT)) < 4 for the full Bullach-Honnor-normalized Mazur-Tate element theta_K^MT of K at its actual conductor m (Definition 2.2, total real period Omega^+ = 2*omega_1), then Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity] = 0.

title: Minimum character depth, minimum unit-witness length and Selmer dimension agree up to p - 1
statement: For every good prime p >= 5 let d_p := dim_{F_p} Sel_p(E/Q); let r_p be the minimum number of distinct Kato primes supporting a mod-p unit Kurihara quantity (B.21); and let h_p be the minimum lambda-valuation (lambda = zeta_p - 1) of chi(theta_K), where theta_K is the full Bullach-Honnor-normalized Mazur-Tate element of a real cyclic degree-p field K at its actual conductor prime to pN and chi is a faithful character (h_p = +infinity is allowed). Then min(h_p, p - 1) = min(r_p, p - 1) = min(d_p, p - 1). Consequently, for this rank-two E and every good p >= 5: h_p < 4 <=> h_p = 2 <=> r_p = 2 <=> d_p <= 3 <=> Sha(E/Q)[p^infinity] = 0.

title: The two-prime bridge: a two-prime unit witness gives exact character depth two
statement: Let p >= 5 be a good prime, let q_1 != q_2 be Kato primes for p (as in B.20), and suppose delta_{q_1 q_2} is a mod-p unit. Let L be the C_p^2 compositum of the degree-p subfields of Q(mu_{q_1}) and Q(mu_{q_2}), and J = (T_1, T_2) the augmentation ideal of F_p[Gal(L/Q)]. In the total-real-period normalization, theta_L = delta_{q_1 q_2} * T_1 T_2 (mod p, J^3). Every cyclic degree-p quotient of L that is nontrivial on both inertia groups (the diagonal quotient is one) has actual conductor q_1 q_2, and each of its faithful characters has exact depth 2.
